key_insight: This study investigates whether a visual network wired like a fly’s brain can combine robustness with computational efficiency. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so it does not establish a performance advantage or explain the proposed link between adversarial perturbations and perceptual illusions.
problem_solved: Artificial vision systems can require substantial energy and be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations. The paper examines whether biological wiring constraints offer a route to more robust, efficient vision.
method: Study FlyNet, a task-optimized, continuous-time recurrent neural network constrained by the fly visual system’s synaptic connectome.
Benchmark FlyNet against artificial neural networks to assess robustness and computational cost.

impact: The work could help practitioners assess connectome-constrained architectures as an alternative to conventional vision networks. Any claimed robustness or efficiency gains require the complete results.
